content.text: ▪︎irreversible; loss of elastic recoil + ⇡ airway resistance w.in the lungs
▪︎preventable; airway + alveolar abnormalities typically caused by exposure to noxious gases/particles (MC cigarette smoke)
▪︎4th MC cause of death in the US
prod cough for ≥3mo/y for 2+ consecutive years
enlrg of airspaces dist to terminal bronchioles
accompanied by destruction of the airspace walls (w/o fibrosis)
*classically seen in smokers, USU affects the upper lobes
▪︎Chronic obstructive asthma: inflam lung condition w/ airflow obstruct reversible w/ or w/o tx
*subtypes ⍉in most recent GOLD definitions; help understand spectrum of clin manifestations
» hereditary: pts w/ sus COPD should be evaluated for ⍺1-antitrypsin deficiency
▪︎secondhand smoke, enviro toxins, recurrent airway infections
▪︎MC in pts >55yo w/ Hx of smoking

: begins w chronic airway inflam that progresses to emphysema, a condition characterized by irreversible bronchial narrowing & alveolar hyperinflation ⇢ loss of diffusion area → V/Q mismatch w/ resultant hypoxemia & hypercapnia
▪︎also SOB on exertion, wheezing, episodes of ⇡ sputum prod
PE: ⇡ AP diameter, hyperresonance to percussion, ⇣ fremitus, crackles; +/- signs of cor pulmonale (depends on stage)
▪︎also prolonged expiration, ⇣ breath sounds, wheezes; ⇡ AP diameter = severe dz
▪︎Sx usually start 40-50yo; SOB initially only w/ significant exertion → w/ mild + mod activity as dz progresses
▪︎dx: pulm Sx (dyspnea, cough, or sputum) + clin context (smoke) + airflow limitation; spirometry when ⍉alt explanation for Sx
▪︎FEV1/FVC (fraction of FVC exhaled in 1st sec) = most helpful to detect airflow limitation in COPD + asthma; cannot determine severity
▪︎tested, given a bronchodilator, + retested ⇢ often little to no improvement in spirometry
▪︎FEV1 ⇣: sm airway inflam + alveolar destruction → air trapping (more energy to exhale, lungs ⍉fully empty)
▪︎FVC may also be ⇣, but ⍉to the extent of FEV1 → ratio <0.7
▪︎⇣FEV1/FVC that returns to nl w/ bronchodilator = asthma (⍉return to nl = COPD)
▪︎nl FEV1/FVC + FEV1 >80% predicted = nl; nl FEV1/FVC + FVC 70-80% predicted → poor technique or obese body habitus
▪︎⇣ DLCO: establishes presence of emphysema (norm in chronic bronchitis)
▪︎low DLCO = measure of the amount of emphysematous destruction (dilated + destroyed alveoli → ⇣ diffusing capacity); high DLCO ⍉COPD
▪︎DLCO ⍉routine; indicated if hypoxemia on pulse ox, breathlessness out of proportion to airflow limitation, or before lung resection
(ex, enlrg lungs, flattened diaphragm, ⇡ AP diameter)
▪︎hyperinflation = MC radiographic finding: flattened diaphragm, ⇡ retrosternal air space, hyperlucency, rapid tapering of vascular markings
PaO2 ≤55mmHg = an indication for cont supplemental O2
➁ Assessment of airflow limitation (% of predicted FEV1 ⇢ GOLD)
➂ Sx/exacerbation Hx (mMRC dyspnea scale, CAT score)
*ICS should only be used in combo w/ LABA/LAMA
▪︎albuterol + ipratropium often used together; still Sxtomatic on a short-acting → add a long-acting bronchodilator (⍉another short-acting)
▪︎starting a LAMA → d/c ipratropium (SAMA): avoid 2 muscarinic antagonists concurrently (dry mouth, urinary retention, blurred vision)
▪︎ICS (ex, budesonide): only once already on a long-acting bronchodilator + still Sxtomatic (⍉if only on ipratropium)
▪︎theophylline: potent bronchodilator for refractory cases; ⍉commonly used (narrow therapeutic index, toxicity SEs)
▪︎SABA PRN for dyspnea; maintenance = combo: dual LABA + LAMA or triple LABA-LAMA-ICS (GOLD by severity)
▪︎mortality benefit directly prop to # of hrs O2 = used
▪︎LTOT = COPD therapy shown to improve survival
▪︎vaccines ⇣ infections + exacerbations; Tdap once as adult if ⍉previously given, then Td or Tdap booster q10y
▪︎tx by Sx severity; smoke cessation = foundation; also inhaled bronchodilators, O2, pulm rehab, NIV; abx for severe dz, infect, or ventilation
▪︎severe COPD: poor prognosis; consider palliative care at end of life (dyspnea can be very uncomfortable + upsetting)
▪︎acute worsening of resp Sx necessitating additional therapy
: advanced age, productive cough, longer duration of COPD, Hx of ABX therapy, COPD hsp w.in past yr, chronic mucous hypersecretion, eosinophil count >340cells/µL, ⊕comorbidities (ex, IHD, HF, DM)
: exclude PNA, PTX, pulm edema, pleural effusion
▪︎azithromycin = abx w/ anti-inflam properties in the lungs
▪︎HFNC O2 therapy, NIPPV, intubation & mech ventilation
